title: Async/Await: Task vs ValueTask in C#

scenes.line2: But when do you use ValueTask?
scenes.say: Async programming in C sharp seems simple, but do you know when to use ValueTask instead of Task?

scenes.label: Task
scenes.sub: Represents an async operation. Most async APIs use Task.
scenes.say: Task is the standard for representing asynchronous work. Most async methods return a Task.

scenes.label: ValueTask
scenes.sub: Used when results may be ready synchronously. Avoids extra allocation.
scenes.say: ValueTask is handy when your method often finishes right away, so you skip creating a new Task object.
Using ConfigureAwait with false avoids capturing the synchronization context. This prevents deadlocks and speeds up library code.

scenes.question: What causes deadlocks in async code?
scenes.right: Blocking on async results without ConfigureAwait can deadlock UI or web threads.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: blocking on async results without ConfigureAwait can freeze your UI or web thread.
